findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Chimney Swift with a slender cigar-shaped body, long narrow curved folded wings, short stiff-tipped tail, dark gray-brown plumage, paler throat, large visible eye, short broad-based bill, and tiny grasping feet.
The corrected upper leg now visibly originates from the ventral lower-body/pelvic region near the other leg and reaches the vertical surface without emerging from the wing or mid-flank.

The primary specimen has one head, one bill, two anatomically coherent folded wings, two legs with gripping feet, and one tail. The detached wing and head studies are clearly supplementary and anatomically consistent with the main specimen.

All visible taxonomy, measurement, habitat, behavior, field-mark, palette, and schematic labels are legible and correctly spelled. The displayed 4.7–5.9 in length, 0.6–1.1 oz weight, and 10.6–11.8 in wingspan ranges match the All About Birds account.

Audubon publishes a somewhat broader wingspan range of 11–12.6 in, but the displayed range is directly supported by All About Birds; the available direct sources do not establish a two-source profile conflict.

The body-length diagram increases correctly from 4.7 in at the bottom to 5.9 in at the top, uses matching metric conversions, contains no contradictory marker, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
